ns2:section.sectionText: This Cline seminar examines the conceptual issues associated with citizenship and immigration, considering current political debates from a variety of perspectives, empirical, historical, and normative. The majority of the course will focus on the United States, but we will also examine the immigration and citizenship practices of other nations as well. Among the topics to be considered include why people migrate; consequences of migration; efforts to integrate immigrants?socially, culturally, and politically?into their host societies; public opinion about immigration and immigrants; various citizenship traditions and rationales; membership, belonging, and national identity; and postnational citizenship. Students will have the opportunity to meet and network with alumni during the Cline Symposium held in the Spring.
ns2:section.sectionNotes: Not intended for students with Freshman class standing.
